history.summary: A non-sectarian temple inspired by Dada Bhagwan (A. M. Patel, 1908–1988), founder of the Akram Vignan movement; it is the first and largest of the Trimandirs. Conceived as a 'three-temples-in-one' for impartial reverence, it gives Jainism, Shaivism and Vaishnavism (plus other deities) equal status on the same platform. The two-storey pink-sandstone structure has a 33-metre central shikhar; the ground floor holds a large discourse hall (satsang hall for 6,000+), the temple shrine is on the first floor. The central sanctum houses a 3.9-metre (13-ft) marble idol of Simandhar Swami with Chandrayan Yaksh and Panchanguli Yakshini, surrounded by Tirthankara and dev/devi idols. The complex also includes a museum and mini-theatre on Dada Bhagwan's life, book store, food zone and children's area. NOTE: although it centres on a Jain Tirthankara, it is not a Jain temple — it is explicitly non-sectarian.

name: Trimandir, Adalaj
town_description: A town in Gandhinagar district on the Ahmedabad–Mehsana highway, about 18 km from Gandhinagar. Famous for the Adalaj stepwell, a five-storey intricately carved vav built in 1499 by Queen Rudabai.
